checked_sources: Frozen verify.py, including the bounded optimizer search and exact small-torus trace calculation
correctness.rationale: The frozen optimizer localization is not justified: the two axial lower bounds and the O(log n) normalized trial cost give only t_n=O(log n) and t_n=Ω(1/log n), not a fixed compact interval for differentiating the compact-uniform Green-function expansion. The repaired proof uses strict convexity in u=Pt/(Pt+Q), where the weighted Laplacian is affine, and positive-definite trace inverse strictly convex. Fixed tests at a<t_0<b both have strictly larger leading costs than t_0, and convexity traps the true optimum between them. An arbitrary bracket yields convergence, and a fixed bracket licenses uniform differentiation. The repair also distinguishes the two endpoint layers: each contributes A(t)[coth(π√t m)−1]/(2m), not the combined contribution; with m=min(j,n−j) the bound O_K((1+m)^2 exp(−c_K m)/m) holds through two derivatives. Reconstructing the resolvent by the Poisson kernel, subtracting the singular endpoint model, and summing the exponential correction verifies A(t)=1/(2π√t) and the displayed C(t). Stationarity and g''(t_0)=P/(4πt_0^(3/2)) give shift coefficient −4πt_0^(3/2)[C(t_0)+2t_0C'(t_0)], which simplifies to the displayed κ. The leading cost changes quadratically in the shift, so the trace constant is 2QC(t_0). Strict convexity and edge-class symmetry still handle unrestricted allocations and n=3; deleting a whole edge class disconnects, P=Q is exactly symmetric, and the unordered pair sum is n² times the trace. The corrected final proof retains the original theorem and requires no numerical certification. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The numerical search in verify.py is confined to a prescribed range and is not evidence of asymptotic localization. The bracket proof supplies that step.
No new test replay or formal proof-assistant certificate. Prices and budget must be fixed and positive.

value.rationale: The natural design objective asks which direction to favor when conductance costs differ, with every edge independently available for investment. The leading optimum splits expenditure equally between directions, but the explicit κ resolves a systematic slow finite-size deviation and quantifies its dependence on price. The second trace term supplies a comparably precise attainable performance benchmark. Neither is a rephrasing of the leading-log fixed-network bound.
residual_risks: No varying-price asymptotic, alternative objective, or rectangular-torus claim.
